decisions.reason: Because it extends the firm's core wafer-substrate capabilities and likely required meaningful process investment, management would tend to continue it and attribute any weak uptake to a still-developing application market.

As a close-to-core carrier wafer offering for a clear handling problem, it fits the firm's stated direction and is the kind of incremental product management would be reluctant to abandon after launch.

This flagship Cu-interposer wafer was publicly launched at a major industry event and tied to the firm's strategic direction, so escalation of commitment strongly favors continued support despite uncertainty.

The off-the-shelf Wafer Universe brand was presented as a flagship multi-model line, making the public commitment and organizational investment high enough that management would be inclined to persist.

Glass-based circuit boards are relatively distant from the firm's established substrate business, so despite prior development spending management is more likely to cut this product and redeploy resources to core wafer offerings and nearer-term projects.
